literal: All lives that have flesh as their basis; nobility has as its basis the virtue called shame.
translation: Just as all physical life depends on the flesh for its existence, perfect nobility depends on the virtue called a sense of shame.
modern: உடலை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டுதான் எல்லா உயிர்களும் வாழ்கின்றன; அதுபோல, சால்பு என்னும் சான்றாண்மை நாணம் என்னும் நற்பண்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது.
explanation: This couplet draws a beautiful analogy between physical existence and moral character. Every living being in the world requires a physical body of flesh to exist. In the exact same way, a person's perfect character or nobility (sālpu) cannot exist without the foundational virtue of 'nāṇ' (a healthy sense of shame or dread of doing wrong). The poet emphasizes that just as a soul without a body cannot manifest, nobility without a sense of shame is impossible.
